assessments.reasoning: Sections 1 and 3.3 constrain the governed language to 4.60, require the corresponding shader version declaration, place it before non-comment and non-whitespace content, and supply core when 460 is written without a profile.

challenge.method: Compare a leading comment followed by the directive, a leading preprocessor definition before the directive, an omitted directive, an explicit compatibility token, the ES 300 and 310 cases, and the separate SPIR-V route.
challenge.results: A leading comment is allowed and a preceding definition breaches the position rule. An omitted directive selects the documented 1.10 fallback, not 4.60. A written compatibility token is not defaulted to core. The separate ES cases require the ES profile token and do not alter the version-460 case. The source treats SPIR-V generation as a toolchain mode.

limitations: This controls GLSL in the stated native desktop OpenGL compilation context. The supported language versions of a specific API context, the language of older directives, and SPIR-V tooling are separate questions.
